config.title: Cookie-Based Auth Flow

intro.title: Cookie-Based Auth Flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that implements a cookie-based authentication flow. You will learn how to manage user login and logout states using Angular services and HTTP interceptors. The core concept involves handling HTTP requests and responses to securely send and receive authentication cookies. You will work with Angular components, services, and TypeScript to create a functional login system. By the end, you'll understand how to protect routes and maintain user sessions using cookies in a web application.
intro.usecase: Cookie-based authentication is the foundation of session management in countless web applications. When you log into platforms like Gmail, GitHub, or online banking dashboards, a secure cookie stores your session token, keeping you authenticated across page refreshes and browser tabs. As a developer, you'll implement this flow in admin panels, e-commerce user accounts, and internal tools where persistent login state is required without exposing tokens in client-side code. This pattern ensures secure, seamless user experiences while maintaining stateless server architecture.

objectives: Implement an Angular service to handle HTTP requests with cookie-based authentication
Configure Angular HTTP interceptors to automatically include authentication cookies in requests
Construct login and logout components that interact with the authentication service
Initialize and manage authentication state using Angular services and RxJS
Apply route guards to protect specific routes based on authentication status
Bind authentication state to UI components to conditionally display content
Manipulate HTTP headers and options to work with cookie-based authentication endpoints

steps.title: Import Angular modules and services needed for cookie-based authentication
steps.instruction: Import Component, Injectable, HttpClient, HttpClientModule, and FormsModule from their respective Angular packages.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your TypeScript file. Component and Injectable come from '@angular/core', HttpClient and HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http', and FormsModule from '@angular/forms'.

steps.hint: Use the @Injectable() decorator above the class definition and add a constructor parameter of type HttpClient.

steps.title: Define login method in AuthService
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthService class, add a login method that takes username and password parameters and returns an Observable. The method should send a POST request to '/api/login' with the credentials in the request body.
steps.hint: Use the HttpClient's post method to make the HTTP request. Remember to include the credentials in the request body as an object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService will have a login method that can be called to authenticate users via a POST request to the server.
successCriteria: AuthService contains a login method with username and password parameters that returns an Observable from http.post to '/api/login'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your login method accepts username and password parameters and returns the http.post Observable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login method is missing or doesn't match the expected signature. It should take username and password parameters and return an Observable from http.post.

steps.title: Define logout method in AuthService
steps.instruction: Add a logout method to your AuthService class that sends a POST request to '/api/logout' and returns an Observable.
steps.hint: The method should be similar to the login method but without credentials. Use the HttpClient's post method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService will have a logout method that sends a POST request to clear authentication cookies.
successCriteria: The AuthService contains a logout method that returns an Observable from a POST request to '/api/logout'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a logout method, but ensure it sends a POST request to '/api/logout' and returns an Observable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout method is missing or incorrect. It should send a POST request to '/api/logout' and return an Observable.

steps.title: Define checkAuth method in AuthService
steps.instruction: In your AuthService class, add a method named checkAuth that sends a GET request to '/api/check-auth' and returns an Observable.

steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService will have a checkAuth method that returns an Observable from a GET request to the authentication check endpoint.
successCriteria: The AuthService contains a checkAuth method that returns this.http.get('/api/check-auth').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your method is named checkAuth and returns the HTTP GET request to '/api/check-auth'.

steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component class named 'AuthComponent' with the @Component decorator. In the constructor, inject the AuthService as a dependency.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component and include AuthService in the constructor parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new AuthComponent class is created with proper component decorator and service injection.
successCriteria: AuthComponent class exists with @Component decorator and constructor injecting AuthService.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the @Component decorator and AuthService injection in the constructor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used @Component and injected AuthService in the constructor.

steps.instruction: In your AuthComponent class, add four properties: username (string), password (string), isAuthenticated (boolean), and userInfo (object with name and email string properties). Use appropriate TypeScript type annotations.
steps.hint: Define these properties directly in the class body, similar to how you would declare variables with types in TypeScript.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthComponent class will have typed properties to track authentication state and user data.
successCriteria: AuthComponent has username (string), password (string), isAuthenticated (boolean), and userInfo (object with name and email) properties with proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but make sure all four are present with correct TypeScript types: username (string), password (string), isAuthenticated (boolean), and userInfo (object with name and email).

steps.title: Build login form template with two-way binding
steps.instruction: In your AuthComponent's template, create a login form with two input fields for username and password using [(ngModel)] for two-way binding, and a login button that calls the onLogin method.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template-driven forms syntax. Remember to import FormsModule in your module for ngModel to work.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthComponent will have a template with a login form containing username and password inputs bound to component properties via [(ngModel)], and a login button that triggers the onLogin method.
successCriteria: The template contains a form with two input fields using [(ngModel)] and a login button with (click)="onLogin()".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both input fields with [(ngModel)] and the login button properly wired to the onLogin method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't match the requirements. Check that you have a form with username and password inputs using [(ngModel)] and a login button that calls onLogin.

steps.title: Add conditional UI for authenticated state
steps.instruction: In your AuthComponent template, add *ngIf directives to conditionally show the login form when not authenticated, and show a welcome message with logout button when authenticated.
steps.hint: Use *ngIf="!isLoggedIn" on the login form and *ngIf="isLoggedIn" on the authenticated content. Remember to include the logout button in the authenticated section.
